findings.title: Device limit check is racy: count-then-insert is not atomic
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the limit by running CountDevices and then conditionally inserting. Two (or more) concurrent anonymous requests for new devices can both observe count < deviceLimit and both insert, exceeding the configured limit. On a busy instance with many simultaneous first-time anonymous visitors, the limit can be breached by an arbitrary margin. Enforcement needs to be atomic (e.g., insert guarded by a transaction with a locked count, a UNIQUE/sequence-based cap, or accepting the race and documenting it).

findings.title: Known device older than 30 days is rejected as 'device limit reached'
findings.body: When the limit is reached, updateDevice only updates rows whose updated_at is within [now-30d, now+1m] and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when 0 rows are affected. The cleanup job (DeleteDevicesOlderThan) only deletes devices older than 61 days, so a device whose last update is between 30 and 61 days old still occupies a row (and is counted by CountDevices) but cannot be updated — its owner gets a hard 'device limit reached' auth error even though refreshing that existing device would not increase the device count. The update branch should fall back to checking whether the device row exists (and update it) before concluding the limit blocks the request.

findings.title: ErrDeviceLimitReached aborts anonymous authentication with a raw internal error
findings.body: TagDevice is now called synchronously in Authenticate, and ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned as the authenticate error. The authn framework will treat this as a failed authentication, so every request from a new anonymous device (once the limit is hit) fails with an unhandled internal error rather than a controlled response (e.g., a 429 or a rendered 'device limit reached' page). The error message 'device limit reached' is also a bare fmt.Errorf with no user-facing wording, and browsers will keep retrying, generating error noise. The authn error handling for this case (status code, redirect behavior, user message) should be explicitly implemented and tested.

findings.title: Local cache is populated before the store write, so a rejected/failed tag is not retried for 29 minutes
findings.body: tagDeviceUI calls localCache.SetDefault(key, ...) before CreateOrUpdateDevice. If CreateOrUpdateDevice fails (including ErrDeviceLimitReached or a transient DB error), the cache entry remains and subsequent requests from the same device skip the store entirely for up to 29 minutes. With the new synchronous error path this means a transient DB failure during the limit check or insert silently stops device tracking, and TagDevice returns an error to the caller on the first attempt but nil on subsequent ones, giving inconsistent auth behavior. Only populate the cache after a successful store call, or evict on error.

findings.title: Extra COUNT query on every device tag when a limit is configured
findings.body: When deviceLimit > 0, every CreateOrUpdateDevice call performs a full COUNT(*) over anon_device filtered by updated_at before deciding whether to insert. For known devices this count is wasted work (the upsert would have succeeded anyway), and without an index on updated_at this is a table scan per new/refreshing device. Consider only doing the count when the upsert would create a new row, or checking existence of the device_id first.

findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit is always serialized and typed inconsistently with the frontend
findings.body: The Go DTO field AnonymousDeviceLimit is a plain int64 with no omitempty, so the JSON payload always contains "anonymousDeviceLimit": 0 even when no limit is configured, while the TypeScript type in packages/grafana-data declares it as `number | undefined`. Consumers cannot distinguish 'no limit configured' from 'limit of 0' except by the 0-as-unset convention, which is undocumented. Either make it a pointer/omitempty or type the frontend field as a plain number and document the 0 = unlimited convention.

findings.title: New device_limit option is not added to sample config or docs
findings.body: The new [auth.anonymous] device_limit setting is parsed but is not added to conf/sample.ini (or defaults.ini comments), so administrators have no discoverable documentation of the option, its default (0 = unlimited), or its semantics (limit over a rolling 30-day window). The PR description also leaves the docs checkbox unchecked.
